live.name: GOLD HARVEST
live.headline: GOLD HARVEST: a threat actor tracked under several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists GOLD HARVEST under five other names and names three remote-access tools tied to it. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: The catalogue record, sourced to Secureworks, tracks the actor as GOLD HARVEST.
The same record lists these aliases: Octo Tempest, Roasted 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Scattered Spider and UNC3944.
The record lists three tools: AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and Logmein.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: GOLD HARVEST
next.headline: GOLD HARVEST (Scattered Spider): phone-based social engineering aimed at help desks and outsourcers
next.in_short: GOLD HARVEST is the Secureworks name for the group also called Scattered Spider. Vendors describe a financially motivated actor that talks its way past help desks and multi-factor checks.

sentences.t: The catalogue record, sourced to Secureworks, lists GOLD HARVEST under the aliases Octo Tempest, Roasted 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Scattered Spider and UNC3944.
CrowdStrike's profile calls SCATTERED SPIDER a prolific eCrime adversary. It describes financially motivated activity since early 2022.
Check Point Research describes the group as active since at least 2022. It says the members are primarily young people aged 19 to 22 from the US and UK.
ReliaQuest describes a financially motivated gang associated with the wider hacking collective known as The Com.

In August 2025 a Telegram brand called Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters borrowed the names of Scattered Spider, ShinyHunters and LAPSUS$. Trustwave SpiderLabs reads it as a situational alliance, not a formal merger.
CrowdStrike says early campaigns reportedly targeted customer relationship management and business-process outsourcing firms. It adds telecommunications and technology companies.
ReliaQuest says 70% of the group's targets belong to the technology, finance and retail trade sectors.
Halcyon says the group compromises call centres and other outsourcing providers to reach many victims at once. It says attacks on UK retail and US insurance likely began, at least in part, this way.
Check Point says the group is now also targeting aviation. It notes the link to airline attacks rests on media reports and intelligence advisories.
Mandiant reports that UNC3944 targets IT help desks to get around multifactor authentication.
ReliaQuest says the group mainly relies on phishing frameworks such as Evilginx and on voice phishing. It also reports typosquatted domains used to bypass multifactor authentication.
BleepingComputer's report lists phishing, SIM swapping and MFA bombing among the group's tactics.
Halcyon says the group leans on insider recruitment and that operators pose as IT staff. It says victims are guided to install remote access tools such as AnyDesk or ScreenConnect.
The catalogue record lists AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and Logmein among the tools.
Rapid7 investigated an April 2026 intrusion that began with a Microsoft Teams message from a fake IT Support account. It says this mirrors Octo Tempest-style tradecraft, and does not confirm a link.

BleepingComputer's report says that in September 2023 the group breached MGM Resorts after impersonating an employee. It says over 100 VMware ESXi hypervisors were then encrypted with BlackCat ransomware.
The same report says the group has partnered with ransomware operations including RansomHub, Qilin and DragonForce.

In May 2025 a wave of attacks hit UK retailers including Marks & Spencer, Co-op and Harrods. ReliaQuest says nothing definitive has tied these incidents to the group, though their coordinated nature hints at a broader campaign.
Check Point cites media reports linking the group to the July 2025 Qantas breach, which affected six million customers.

After an Aflac breach disclosure, a spokesperson could not attribute it to a group. BleepingComputer says it shows all the signs of Scattered Spider, and Google's John Hultquist is quoted saying the group has been breaching US insurers.
ReliaQuest reports arrests of at least five alleged members in 2024. It says these did little to slow the group's partnerships.
Treat help-desk requests to reset passwords or multifactor methods as high risk, and confirm the caller through a separate, trusted channel.
Review what outsourced support providers and contractors can reach in your systems, and watch their access closely.
